text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] performance_anomaly: service=model-server-prod route=/v1/chat p95 latency jumped above 700ms (SLO=400ms) — detected 2025-11-13T08:04:02Z. Affected region: eu-central-1.

sam (oncall): taking lead. Paging rotation 2. I see spike on p50 too (was ~60ms now ~180ms). Any deploys or infra changes in last 2h?

nina (sre): checking cluster events and infra-change logs. kube-deploy shows kernel image rollout job finished for nodepool-gpu-euc1 at 07:20 UTC (kernel 6.3.7 -> 6.5.1) applied to 6/18 nodes. No app deploys.

kai (ml infra): tracing ingest: observability-bot: trace set https://traces.redwood/internal/trace/ef12bb (high-latency sample). Tokenization spans unaffected; bulk of delay occurs in pre-GPU scheduling window.

observability-bot: Aggregated metrics: p50 increased at 07:58, p95 spike begins 08:02. CPU runqueue length and context-switch rate increased on upgraded nodes.

cs-rep: raising customer impact: 3 customers reported UI lag for model chat; no API errors. CS teams notified.

sam (oncall): hypothesis tracker (in-thread):
  - H1: kernel scheduler changes in 6.5.1 introduced longer wakeup latency for threads pinned to CPU which our inference worker pattern exposes.
  - H2: irq/softirq steering or irqbalance misconfiguration causing excessive softirq on CPU hot cores.
  - H3: userspace change (unlikely, no deploy) or model variant causing micro-stalls.

nina (sre): collecting artifacts: dmesg, /var/log/kern.log, perf counters (context-switch, irq, softirq, cpu-migrations), and /proc/interrupts snapshots. Uploading to GCS: gs://redwood-ops/incidents/1712108642/artifacts.tar.gz

sam (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) temporarily route 15% traffic to fallback-model-small; 2) scale up replicas in eu cluster +25%; 3) run targeted canary rollback on a single upgraded node to previous kernel and observe.

kernel-bot: Kernel deployment note: 6.5.1 includes scheduler patches RQ balancing and group scheduling tweaks (changelog refs: https://kernel.org/6.5.1/changes).

kai (ml infra): posting quick trace excerpt (snip):
```
span: request_receive 2ms
span: pre_gpu_work_queue 18ms -> 240ms (p95)
span: gpu_submit 5ms
```

nina (sre): dmesg snippet from node-gpu-22 (upgraded):
```
[08:01:14] kernel: rcu_preempt detected stalls on CPU 3
[08:01:14] kernel: softirq took 54ms
[08:01:14] kernel: sched: wake_up took 37ms
```

sam (oncall): good signal. Anybody see similar on nodes NOT upgraded?

observability-bot: nodes without upgrade (node-gpu-05, gpu-09) show stable p95 ~130ms and no dmesg stalls. Correlation strong with kernel upgrade.

nina (sre): perf top on node-gpu-22 shows high time in kernel 'do_softirq' and 'try_to_wake_up' and userland futex_wait queues. Perf counters attached: gs://.../perf_node22.csv

kai (ml infra): quick run of /proc/interrupts shows RTX interrupt affinity concentrated on CPU 3 and 4; irqbalance was enabled but seems to have assigned affinity poorly after reboot. Could be related to vendor driver+kernel interaction.

sam (oncall): immediate mitigations applied:
  - scaled replicas +25% at 08:12 UTC
  - routing 15% traffic to fallback-model-small at 08:13 UTC
  - temporarily set irqbalance=0 and manually redistributed GPU interrupts on node-gpu-22 at 08:20 UTC (pin to CPU 0-1).

observability-bot: after manual irq pinning on node-gpu-22 p95 improved from 820ms -> 420ms within 2m; cluster-wide remained elevated until further action.

cs-rep: customers saw partial relief after scale + fallback, but still some UI lag for heavier chat sessions.

sam (oncall): rolling canary rollback start on node-gpu-22 to kernel 6.3.7 at 08:30. Will cordon/drain and reboot. Expect 6-8m.

nina (sre): collecting baseline perf counters pre-rollback for comparison. Also running 'perf record' on a synthetic load to reproduce.

kai (ml infra): note: we also observed slight drop in KV cache hit-rate on traces (~3%) around same time; could increase token overhead but not enough to explain p95 delta alone. Adding to hypotheses as amplification factor.

kernel-bot: vendor kernel changelog highlights: changes to wakeup path and preempt accounting in 6.5.x series. Recommend vendor/kernel-team ticket if confirmed.

observability-bot: post-rollback metrics for node-gpu-22 at 08:38: p50 back to 70ms, p95 = 140ms. Nodes still on 6.5.1 remain high.

sam (oncall): strong signal for kernel causing tails. Proposal: staggered rollback in 2-node batches with canaries, maintain autoscale and fallback until finish. Notify infra and schedule incident maintenance window.

nina (sre): perf delta summary (node-gpu-22 pre vs post rollback): context-switches per sec 18k -> 5k, softirq time 48% -> 12%, futex_wait avg latency p95 22ms -> 3ms.

kai (ml infra): reproduced locally on a small test: booting a 6.5.1 image on a GPU host with our driver showed irq affinity flapping and increased softirq. Will capture a reproducer and open PR.

sam (oncall): tracking actions in-thread (owners):
  - nina: run batch rollback + produce full perf CSVs and script (due today EOD).
  - kai: reproduce and open kernel/vendor issue with trace/perf artifacts (due tomorrow).
  - cs-rep: customer follow-ups + status (ongoing).
  - sam: coordinate maintenance window and update incident status.

nina (sre): adding runbook note: hold kernel upgrades for GPU nodepools for 48h and run batch perf smoke tests (cpu steal, softirq, context-switch baseline) before automation flips upgrade flag.

cs-rep: updated customers at 09:05 UTC; they appreciate the rollback but asked for root cause timeline and mitigation steps.

sam (oncall): severity downgraded to SEV-2 at 08:50 UTC after rollback canaries showed improvement and staggered rollback plan in flight. We'll produce a full postmortem. Thanks for rapid response. :thumbsup:

nina (sre): uploading artifacts: gs://redwood-ops/incidents/1712108642/{dmesg,perf,proc_interrupts,traces}_v1.tar.gz

kernel-bot: opening vendor bug with summary and attached perf/traces. Ticket #KB-3471.

sam (oncall): closing live incident thread. RCA meeting scheduled tomorrow 14:00 UTC to finalize timeline, root cause (kernel scheduler/irq-affinity change), and long-term mitigations (upgrade gating, perf smoke tests, alert correlation).

observability-bot: Incident 2025-11-13-1712108642 updated: status=mitigated, severity=SEV-2, owner=sam (oncall), artifacts=gs://redwood-ops/incidents/1712108642/.
